facts.text: Gibson Township was officially founded in 1813, carved from northern Clifford Township and named for Judge John Bannister Gibson, future Pennsylvania Supreme Court chief justice.
The first permanent settler, Revolutionary War veteran Joseph Potter, arrived January 21, 1792, and built a cabin near the Bend on Tunkhannock Creek.
Joshua Jay erected Gibson’s first grist‑mill and blacksmith shop in 1794, anchoring the early village that would grow around his log cabins.
During the 1840s and 1850s, lumber from Gibson’s dense forests was floated down the Tunkhannock and Susquehanna Rivers to markets in Harrisburg and Baltimore.
A Little Free Library sits in Gibson, inviting residents and travelers alike to take a book or leave one for the next visitor.
Gibson Township spans roughly 32 square miles and is run by a three‑member board of supervisors, with offices located on State Route 92 in South Gibson.
